A1.justification: Despite the changed title and renaming of CoPatch/CoMap to B2G/P-Map, the authors, core spatial-map approach, and numerous experiments match. Both PDFs, including their equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 Section 4 and Appendix C report original segmentation experiments, component ablations, spatial-map analyses, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original segmentation results and adds automatic-layer-selection experiments, multilingual segmentation and retrieval results, and extensive diagnostic analyses in Sections 3 and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming the retained spatial-map approach, v2 introduces automatic visual-layer selection using tile permutations or cluster coherence, plus multilingual text-layer selection and centroid injection followed by continued encoding. It also presents score-plus-overlap mask reranking. V1 uses fixed visual exit layers and context-augmented text features without these automatic-selection and multilingual components.

E1.justification: The English RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, and PhraseCut coverage is retained. V2 adds nine non-English query languages through translated RefCOCO-family benchmarks and evaluates zero-shot text-to-image retrieval alongside segmentation. These additions substantially expand language and task coverage without implying new underlying image collections.

E2.justification: The main RefCOCO comparisons are substantially revised: v1 includes Region Token, CLIPSurgery, Cropping, TAS, CaR, Ref-Diff, and weakly/pseudo-supervised methods, whereas v2 Tables 1 and S3 concentrate on Global-Local and HybridGL. Some removed comparators remain in other analyses. V2 additionally evaluates multilingual final-layer fusion, translation-based controls, and alternative centroid/anchor strategies.

E3.justification: V2 standardizes its main comparisons around matched segmentors and CT/SG-enhanced baselines, adds SigLIP/SigLIP2 configurations, and introduces multilingual protocols using IoU@50, Recall@1, fixed image features for retrieval controls, and averaging across 90 language/split cases. Its description of calibration as unlabeled conflicts with the retained IoU-based tuning in Appendix C.4, so an actual change to calibration supervision is not established.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct negation-versus-clustering ablations in Table 3c, automatic-layer-selection distributions, and extensive multilingual diagnostics. These test translation quality, intervention depth, global versus instance-specific centroids, anchor language, fusion strength, and residual grounding failures. Existing mask-generator, context-token, exit-layer, and fusion analyses are largely retained and reorganized.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly labels improvements statistically significant in Tables 1 and S3 and describes a nonsignificant reranking difference in Appendix A.4. V1 lacks equivalent statistical annotations. Neither version documents a significance-testing procedure, repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals, so this establishes changed reporting rather than demonstrated additional statistical validation.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial automatic-selection, multilingual segmentation, retrieval, and diagnostic results while removing many top-3 result rows. The fixed CLIP ViT-B/16 main results are retained, but CLIP ViT-B/32 with Mask2Former on RefCOCOg validation changes from 52.24 to 53.47 mIoU under revised method reporting, not an established identical-setting gain. Figure 6c also assigns 28.68/29.14 to LAVT, although v1 Table 2 attributes those PhraseCut scores to Pseudo-RIS.

T1.justification: V2 adds mathematical definitions for permutation-based positional sensitivity, cross-language consistency, cluster response contrast and compactness, and the resulting layer-selection objectives. These substantially extend the formal method specification beyond v1's patch similarity and clustering formulation. The cosine-negation identity is retained; no new theorem or correctness proof is supplied.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contributions on context-token augmentation, efficient spatial-map extraction, and improved zero-shot segmentation. V2 reframes the contribution around coupled positional and multilingual biases at the final-layer interface, a unified probe–select–ground framework, and improvements extending to multilingual retrieval. The latent spatial-information claim remains, but the central scientific scope broadens substantially.

C2.justification: V2 develops new explanations involving language-dependent geometric drift, intervention depth, and instance-specific multilingual stabilization rather than translation quality alone. It adds concrete limitations concerning parallel translated queries at inference, increased latency, and remaining directional or role-assignment failures. The earlier spatial-guidance and spatial-map limitations remain in Appendix F.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation and reproducibility information, including multilingual benchmark provenance and input-access conventions, SigLIP-specific normalization, additional hardware assignments, and latency measurement boundaries, CUDA synchronization, and batch size. Existing fixed-layer hyperparameters remain in the appendix. Conversely, v1's explicit code URL and supplementary code/data availability statement are absent from v2; this establishes lost access information, not that the resources themselves disappeared.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around multilingual encoders and training-free cross-language stabilization, adding discussion and citations such as MURAL, UC2, mCLIP, SigLIP2, and Nogueira et al.'s translated benchmark. It presents B2G as complementary to multilingual pretraining and distillation, extending v1's predominantly segmentation-focused positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, methodology narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around representational bias. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 4, detailed context-token material moves into the appendix, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded from A–D to A–F. These changes substantially alter the document's narrative and structure.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the opening illustration and framework diagram, restructures the main comparison tables by backbone and segmentor, and adds averages and significance highlighting. It introduces multilingual performance/cost plots, diagnostic heatmaps, and retrieval examples. Existing figures are also consolidated or relocated, including the hyperparameter plots combined into Figure S13.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens experimental attribution through matched-segmentor comparisons, direct design ablations, and multilingual controls, while clarifying translation requirements and inference costs. However, it introduces material reporting problems: Table 2's RefCOCOg language scores average 48.16 Recall@1 rather than the reported 50.16; the unlabeled-calibration description conflicts with Appendix C.4's IoU-based tuning; and significance claims lack a documented test. These problems affect confidence in central comparisons, preventing a reliable net quality judgment despite the stronger analyses.
